blocks.caption: Three kinds of neuron
rows: outside the CNS, in clusters called ganglia
unipolar: one long dendrite whose end branches to the receptors, and an axon
multipolar: many branching dendrites, a long axon
short axons forming local circuits, or long axons linking distant regions

blocks.text: Inter-neurons receive impulses from sensory neurons or other inter-neurons and pass them to motor neurons or other inter-neurons. Those with short axons form circuits with nearby neurons to analyse small pieces of information; those with long axons connect different regions of the brain and spinal cord.

blocks.alt: One pathway of three neurons: a sensory neuron with receptor endings at the left, its cell body on a side branch and a myelinated axon, passes the impulse to an inter-neuron, which passes it to a motor neuron whose myelinated axon ends at an effector. Small arrows show the direction of the impulse from receptor to effector.
